Weyl metal is the first example of a conducting material with a nontrivialelectronic structure topology, making it distinct from an ordinary metal.Unlike in insulators, the nontrivial topology is not related to invariants,associated with completely filled bands, but with ones, associated with theFermi surface. The Fermi surface of a topological metal consists ofdisconnected sheets, each enclosing a Weyl node, which is a point of contactbetween two nondegenerate bands. Such a point contact acts as a source of Berrycurvature, or a magnetic monopole in momentum space. Its charge, or the flux ofthe Berry curvature through the enclosing Fermi surface sheet, is a topologicalinvariant. We review the current state of this rapidly growing field, with afocus on bulk transport phenomena in topological metals.

Controlled chemical transformation of nanostructures is a promising techniqueto obtain precisely designed novel materials which are difficult to synthesizeotherwise. We report high-temperature vapor phase anion exchange reactions tochemically transform II-VI semiconductor nanostructures (100-300 nm lengthscale) while retaining the single crystallinity, crystal structure, morphologyand even defect distribution of the parent material via atomic templating. Theconcept of atomic templating is employed to obtain kinetically controlled,thermodynamically metastable structural phases such as zincblende CdSe and CdSfrom zincblende CdTe upon complete chemical replacement of Te with Se or S. Theunderlying transformation mechanisms are explained through first-principlesdensity functional theory calculations. Atomic templating is a unique path toindependently tune materials phase and composition at the nanoscale allowingsynthesis of novel materials.

Quantitative EEG in subcortical neglect.Right-sided capsulo-lenticular strokes may cause left visuo-spatial neglect. The neural mechanism most frequently evoked to account for the occurrence of related cognitive disorders is remote cortical dysfunction in the posterior part of the right hemisphere. We studied 33 patients with capsulo-lenticular stroke, with (n = 16) or without (n = 17) associated subcortical neglect. A 20-channel EEG cartography system was used. Four regions of interest were delineated on the topographic map. Absolute delta and thêta amplitude peaks were obtained, as well as left-to-right ratios between activities in homologous regions of interest. The population was subdivided into two groups according to the presence or absence of neglect. Delta activity was higher in neglect patients than in patients without neglect, but the magnitude of delta activity differences between the two groups of patients did not depend on the site. The left-to-right ratio of delta activity between posterior homologous regions was lower in neglect patients, suggesting that right posterior dysfunction producing an imbalance between these regions might contribute to the emergence of the attention disorder.

Prenatal maternal stress: effects on pregnancy and the (unborn) child.Animal experiments have convincingly demonstrated that prenatal maternal stress affects pregnancy outcome and results in early programming of brain functions with permanent changes in neuroendocrine regulation and behaviour in offspring. To evaluate the existing evidence of comparable effects of prenatal stress on human pregnancy and child development. Data sources used included a computerized literature search of PUBMED (1966-2001); Psychlit (1987-2001); and manual search of bibliographies of pertinent articles. Recent well-controlled human studies indicate that pregnant women with high stress and anxiety levels are at increased risk for spontaneous abortion and preterm labour and for having a malformed or growth-retarded baby (reduced head circumference in particular). Evidence of long-term functional disorders after prenatal exposure to stress is limited, but retrospective studies and two prospective studies support the possibility of such effects. A comprehensive model of putative interrelationships between maternal, placental, and fetal factors is presented. Apart from the well-known negative effects of biomedical risks, maternal psychological factors may significantly contribute to pregnancy complications and unfavourable development of the (unborn) child. These problems might be reduced by specific stress reduction in high anxious pregnant women, although much more research is needed.

A shaft is held in place within a bore of a housing with a band of resilient material that is located between the shaft and the housing and has a series of projections extending radially inwards. The shaft surface has a first part that lies closer to the longitudinal axis of the bore than a second part, when the shaft and housing are assembled. The shaft is initially inserted into the resilient band, which is held within the bore, such that the first part of the shaft surface is oriented towards one of the projections of the resilient band. In this orientation of the shaft, the projection is not compressed. By orienting the second part of the shaft surface, the projection is brought under compression and the shaft is held firmly within the bore.

[Noninvasive head fixation for external irradiation of tumors of the head-neck area].To fully utilize the technical capabilities of radiation diagnostics and planning, a precise and reproducible method of head fixation is a prerequisite. We have adapted the Vogele-Bale-Hohner (VBH) head holder (Wellhöfer Dosimetrie, Schwarzenbruck, Germany), originally designed for frameless stereotactic operations, to the requirements of external beam radiotherapy. A precise and reproducible head fixation is attained by an individualized vacuum upper-dental cast which is connected over 2 hydraulic arms to an adjustable head- and rigid base-plate. Radiation field and patient alignment lasers are marked on a relocatable clear PVC localization box. The possibility of craniocaudal adjustment of the head plate on the base plate allows the system to adapt to the actual position of the patient on the radiotherapy couch granting tensionless repositioning. The VBH head holder has proven itself to be a precise yet practicable method of head fixation. Duration of mouthpiece production and daily repositioning is comparable to that of the thermoplastic mask. The new head holder is in routine use at our hospital and quite suitable for external beam radiation of patients with tumors of the head and neck.

Based on a model of globular cluster self-enrichment published in a previouspaper, we present an explanation for the metallicity gradient observedthroughout the galactic Old Halo. Our self-enrichment model is based on theability of globular cluster progenitor clouds to retain the ejecta of a firstgeneration of Type II Supernovae. The key point is that this ability depends onthe pressure exerted on the progenitor cloud by the surrounding protogalacticmedium and therefore on the location of the cloud in the protoGalaxy. Sincethere is no significant (if any) metallicity gradient in the whole halo, wealso present a review in favour of a galactic halo partly build via accretionsand mergers of satellite systems. Some of them bear their own globular clustersand therefore ``contaminate'' the system of globular clusters formed ``insitu'', namely within the original potential well of the Galaxy. Therefore, thecomparison between our self-enrichment model and the observational data shouldbe limited to the genuine galactic globular clusters, the so-called Old Halogroup.

Spontaneous thoracic spinal subdural hematoma associated with fibromuscular dysplasia.Spontaneous spinal subdural hematoma (SDH) is an uncommon cause of acute spinal cord compression. When it does occur, however, it may have disastrous results and a poor prognosis. The nontraumatic acute spinal SDH usually results from a defect in a hemostatic mechanism (such as coagulopathy or the use of anticoagulant therapy) or from iatrogenic causes (such as spinal puncture). Fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD) is a nonatherosclerotic systemic arteriopathy of unknown cause that typically affects the small and medium arteries in young to middle-aged women. The authors report on their experience with a patient with an acute spontaneous spinal SDH that occurred in conjunction with FMD.

The aim of the present paper is to provide an \emph{intrinsic} investigationof the properties of the most important geometric objects associated with thefundamental linear connections in Finsler geometry. We investigateintrinsically the most general relations concerning the torsion tensor fieldsand the curvature tensor fields associated with a given regular connection onthe pullback bundle of a Finsler manifold. These relations, in turn, play a keyrole in obtaining other interesting results concerning the properties of themost important geometric objects associated with the fundamental canonicallinear connections on the pullback bundle of a Finsler manifold, namely, theCartan connection, the Berwald connection, the Chern (Rund) connection and theHashiguchi connection. For the sake of completeness and for comparison reasons, we provide anappendix presenting a global survey of canonical linear connections in Finslergeometry and the fundamental geometric objects associated with them.

Method and apparatus are described for improving the impact angle between a missile and stationary or moving target in the presence of stationary or adverse wind conditions. A triggered bias detector provides an enabling signal to a bias resolver when the pitch line of sight rate of a missile exceeds a predetermined level. The bias resolver supplies first and second bias signals to the pitch forward guidance loop and yaw forward guidance loop in response to the detected pitch line of sight rate. The missile is given a lofting trajectory in response to the applied bias signal as it closes on the target. Impact angles of a more nearly vertical condition over a wide range of missile/target acquisition geometric conditions are obtained using this triggered bias technique over conventional constant gravity bias proportional guidance techniques.

A circuit structure for implementing the lookup table of a network switching device is provided. With the circuit structure, the memory space of the lookup table could be fully utilized, and the time spent in searching the table is guaranteed to be within a specific time interval. The circuit structure divides the memory space of the lookup table into N blocks, each of which contains L records. The N blocks are directly connected to all search and comparison engines of the M network ports via separate buses respectively. An address generator continuously issues sequential address signals 0, 1, 2 . . . , L−1 to all blocks. Upon receiving an address signal, each block delivers its addressed record to all search and comparison engines via its own bus. A search and comparison engine therefore would compare all N×L records of the lookup table after the address generator has finished a full cycle of issuing L addresses. Searching the lookup table for an incoming packet, in the worst case, wouldn't take up more time than what is required by the address generator to issue a full cycle of L addresses.

Modeling gaze position-dependent opsoclonus.Opsoclonus/flutter (O/F) is a rare disorder of the saccadic system. Previously, we modeled O/F that developed in a patient following abuse of anabolic steroids. That model, as in all models of the saccadic system, generates commands to make a change in eye position. Recently, we saw a patient who developed a unique form of opsoclonus following a concussion. The patient had postsaccadic ocular flutter in both directions of gaze, and opsoclonus during fixation and pursuit in the left hemifield. A new model of the saccadic system is needed to account for this gaze-position dependent O/F. We started with our prior model, which contains two key elements, mutual inhibition between inhibitory burst neurons on both sides and a prolonged reactivation time of the omnipause neurons (OPNs). We included new inputs to the OPNs from the nucleus prepositus hypoglossi and the frontal eye fields, which contain position-dependent neurons. This provides a mechanism for delaying OPN reactivation, and creating a gaze-position dependence. A simplified pursuit system was also added, the output of which inhibits the OPNs, providing a mechanism for gaze-dependence during pursuit. The rest of the model continues to generate a command to change eye position.

Risk adjustment has become an increasingly important tool in healthcare. Ithas been extensively applied to payment adjustment for health plans to reflectthe expected cost of providing coverage for members. Risk adjustment models aretypically estimated using linear regression, which does not fully exploit theinformation in claims data. Moreover, the development of such linear regressionmodels requires substantial domain expert knowledge and computational effortfor data preprocessing. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for riskadjustment that uses semantic embeddings to represent patient medicalhistories. Embeddings efficiently represent medical concepts learned fromdiagnostic, procedure, and prescription codes in patients' medical histories.This approach substantially reduces the need for feature engineering. Ourresults show that models using embeddings had better performance than acommercial risk adjustment model on the task of prospective risk scoreprediction.

The typed letter was sent in September 1965 to Atlanta-based DJ Paul Drew to thank him for his help on the Fab Four's tour of the US. Signed by John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison and Ringo Starr, it was auctioned along with a letter from Beatles' press officer Tony Barrow. They were typed on manager Brian Epstein's NEMS Enterprises notepaper. The letter reads: "Dear Paul, we just thought that we would like to write to you all and say thanks very much for your help on the tour. We enjoyed it and appreciated your patience and co-operation. Hope to see you next year." Auctioneer Andrew Aldridge said it was an "extremely rare" piece of rock and roll history. "Anything signed by all four Beatles is highly collectable, but to have it on NEMS stationery and addressed to Paul Drew - one of architects of Top 40 radio - takes it to another level," he said. The accompanying letter from Mr Barrow confirms details for the group's 1965 tour. The auction house said the lot was sold to an English collector.

The present invention includes an internal combustion engine having at least one piston reciprocating within a cylinder, and an exhaust port allowing communication of the cylinder with an exhaust passage. A moveable shutter is provided to vary the effective area of the exhaust port. The shutter varies the effective area cyclically in a timed relationship to the reciprocal motion of the piston within the cylinder. A sensor is provided to measure an operating characteristic of the engine and to generate signals responding to the operating characteristic sensed. A control unit is provided to process the signals and to control the motion of the shutter in response to the signals.

c-kit mutation and osteopetrosis-like osteopathy in a patient with systemic mast cell disease.We describe the case of a 69-year-old man who presented with persistent skeletal pain and unusual imaging findings. Pseudogout in a young patient. Calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate (CPPD) crystal deposition disease is conventionally classified into cases that are primary and secondary. Primary CPPD disease typically occurs in individuals between the ages of 45 and 65, with a slight predominance in males. However, pseudogout can also occur in younger patients due to various factors.One such factor is the presence of a metabolic disorder, such as hyperparathyroidism or hypothyroidism. These conditions can lead to the accumulation of CPPD crystals in the joint fluid, causing inflammation and pain. Additionally, genetic predisposition can also play a role in the development of pseudogout in younger patients. For instance, certain mutations in the ANKH gene have been linked to an increased risk of developing CPPD disease.In younger patients, pseudogout often presents with acute onset of joint pain and swelling, similar to gout. However, the diagnosis of CPPD disease in this age group can be challenging, as the clinical presentation may overlap with other inflammatory arthropathies. Therefore, a thorough medical evaluation and laboratory tests, including joint fluid analysis, are essential to confirm the diagnosis.

A persistent-mode High Temperature Superconductor (HTS) shim coil is provided having at least one rectangular shaped thin sheet of HTS, wherein the design revolutionizes magnetic field control in high-tech systems. These coils, made from cutting-edge superconducting materials, operate without electrical resistance when cooled, enabling them to maintain a steady current—hence “persistent mode”—without energy loss. The rectangular shape allows for compact, versatile integration into devices like MRI machines or particle accelerators, where precise magnetic field adjustments (“shimming”) are critical. Unlike traditional copper coils that waste energy as heat, HTS shim coils excel at low temperatures (though “high temperature” in this context still means chilly -196°C, achievable with liquid nitrogen). This makes them energy-efficient and space-saving, reducing both costs and environmental footprints. Their reliability under high magnetic fields opens doors for next-gen tech, from medical imaging to fusion reactors. Essentially, it’s a tiny, rectangle-shaped marvel that helps scientists and engineers manipulate magnetic fields with unprecedented precision—all while sipping power like a minimalist’s dream.

The sparse inverse covariance estimation problem is commonly solved using an $\ell_{1}$-regularized Gaussian maximum likelihood estimator known as "graphical lasso." This method aims to identify conditional independence relationships in multivariate data by estimating a sparse precision matrix (the inverse of the covariance matrix). The $\ell_{1}$ penalty encourages sparsity, effectively setting small entries in the precision matrix to zero, which corresponds to edges absent in the underlying graphical model. This approach is widely used in fields like genomics, finance, and social network analysis, where uncovering latent dependencies between variables is critical. The graphical lasso balances model complexity and fit by trading off the likelihood of the data against the sparsity-inducing regularization term. However, solving the optimization problem is computationally challenging due to the non-differentiability of the $\ell_{1}$ penalty. Efficient algorithms, such as coordinate descent and proximal gradient methods, have been developed to address this. Despite its popularity, the method assumes Gaussian-distributed data and may struggle with high-dimensional datasets where the number of variables exceeds sample size. Ongoing research explores alternatives, such as nonparanormal extensions or sparse learning with different penalties, to enhance robustness and scalability. The graphical lasso remains a cornerstone in statistical learning for its simplicity and interpretability in decoding complex relational structures.

We address a simple but fundamental issue arising in the study of graphene, as well as of other systems that have a crystalline structure with more than one atom per unit cell: the definition of "atomicity." While seemingly straightforward, the assignment of local atomistic charges is crucial for understanding material properties, particularly in computational simulations.Current methods often rely on arbitrary partitioning schemes, leading to inconsistencies and hindering direct comparison of theoretical predictions with experimental observations. This ambiguity undermines the predictive power of simulations and limits our ability to design novel materials.We argue for a standardized, physically-motivated definition of atomicity. This should be based on a rigorous quantum mechanical framework, such as the modern theory of polarization, that provides a unique and gauge-invariant description of charge distribution. Until such a consensus is reached, the interpretation of computational results and the progress in materials science will remain hampered by this fundamental, yet unresolved, issue.

There are two types of PDF documents – those created by sending Office files, images, etc. to an Acrobat like PDF printer and those created by scanning something on a flatbed scanner or using your phone's camera. While they look the same, they are completely different under the hood.Print-created PDFs are searchable and selectable. You can copy text, highlight important sections, and easily find specific words. Scan-created PDFs, on the other hand, are basically just pictures. Think of them as digital photographs of a document.This difference matters! Want to quickly find a specific clause in a scanned contract? Good luck! You'll be scrolling through pages, visually searching. Need to copy and paste information from a scanned receipt? Forget about it.Luckily, there's a solution: OCR (Optical Character Recognition). This technology analyzes the image of the scanned document and converts it into editable and searchable text. So, next time you're dealing with a scanned PDF, remember OCR is your friend. It's the key to unlocking the information trapped within!

Feruloylation in grasses: current and future perspectives. A tandem enzymatic approach for detecting and imaging tumor-associated Thomsen-Friedenreich antigen disaccharide (Galactose-β1-3-N-acetylgalactosamine, TF antigen) offers a promising strategy for cancer diagnostics. The TF antigen, a cryptic carbohydrate structure overexpressed on malignant cells, is linked to tumor progression and metastasis. Traditional antibody-based detection methods often suffer from cross-reactivity and low sensitivity. In contrast, this method employs two enzymes: a β-galactosidase to selectively expose the TF epitope by cleaving terminal galactose residues from adjacent glycans, followed by a glycosyltransferase to attach a fluorescent or biotinylated probe for visualization. This sequential enzymatic process enhances specificity, minimizing background noise from non-target glycans. The approach leverages the precision of enzymatic reactions, enabling high-resolution imaging of tumor margins in vitro and in vivo. Additionally, its modular design permits adaptation to various imaging modalities, such as fluorescence microscopy or positron emission tomography. By circumventing reliance on antibodies, this technique reduces variability and improves reproducibility, critical for clinical applications. Such advancements hold potential for early cancer detection, intraoperative guidance, and monitoring therapeutic responses, underscoring the value of enzymatic tools in glycobiology and oncology research. Further validation in preclinical models could accelerate translation into diagnostic platforms.

**Expression of CXCR1 and CXCR2 receptors in malignant melanoma with different metastatic potential and their role in interleukin-8 (CXCL8) signaling have emerged as critical factors in understanding disease progression.** Malignant melanoma, an aggressive skin cancer, exhibits varying metastatic potential, with CXCR1 and CXCR2—key chemokine receptors—implicated in tumor behavior. Recent studies reveal that melanomas with high metastatic potential demonstrate upregulated expression of these receptors compared to less aggressive variants. CXCL8, a pro-inflammatory chemokine, binds to CXCR1/CXCR2, activating downstream pathways such as PI3K/Akt and MAPK, which drive angiogenesis, cell proliferation, and invasion. Elevated receptor expression correlates with enhanced tumor cell survival and immune evasion, underscoring their prognostic significance. Preclinical models targeting CXCR1/CXCR2 show reduced metastasis, highlighting therapeutic potential. However, the complexity of tumor microenvironments necessitates further research to elucidate context-dependent mechanisms. Understanding these interactions may pave the way for novel biomarkers or combination therapies, offering hope for managing advanced melanoma. Thus, CXCR1/CXCR2 modulation represents a promising avenue in precision oncology, warranting continued investigation into their dual roles in metastasis and immune regulation.

Distinctive properties of fucosyl glycopeptides on human teratoma cells are crucial for understanding the complex interactions in tumor biology. Fucose-labeled glycopeptides from four human teratoma cell lines have been studied to elucidate their role in cellular processes such as cell signaling, adhesion, and immune response evasion. These glycopeptides are characterized by the presence of fucose, a hexose deoxy sugar, which is typically linked to glycans on the cell surface proteins. The structural analysis of these fucosylated glycopeptides reveals unique glycan branching patterns, which may contribute to the malignant potential of teratoma cells. These patterns are hypothesized to modulate interactions with the extracellular matrix and affect the binding affinity to lectins, influencing cellular adhesion and migration. Furthermore, the differential expression of fucosyltransferases, the enzymes responsible for attaching fucose to glycans, underscores the importance of fucosylation in cancer progression. Understanding these distinctive properties could lead to novel therapeutic targets for combating teratoma and other related malignancies.

We consider the problem of optimizing combinatorial spaces (e.g., sequences, trees, and graphs) using expensive black-box function evaluations. For example, this arises in drug discovery where evaluating a molecule's efficacy requires costly lab experiments. Traditional optimization methods often fail due to the discrete nature of the search space and the lack of gradient information.Bayesian Optimization (BO) offers a principled approach by modeling the objective function as a Gaussian Process. This allows BO to balance exploration (sampling uncertain regions) and exploitation (sampling promising regions). Key to BO's success is the acquisition function, which guides the search by quantifying the utility of evaluating a particular point.However, applying BO to combinatorial spaces requires careful consideration of the kernel function, which defines similarity between different structures. Specialized kernels, such as graph kernels or string kernels, are often necessary to capture the underlying structure of the space and ensure effective optimization. The computational cost of these kernels can also be a limiting factor.

# New STI Technology Paves Way for Advanced Semiconductor DevicesA shallow trench isolation (STI) structure (170, 300), formed in a silicon substrate (110) for use in sub-micron semiconductor devices, represents a significant advancement in integrated circuit technology. Engineers at leading semiconductor research facilities have developed this improved isolation technique to replace conventional methods as device dimensions continue to shrink.The STI structure effectively isolates adjacent transistors, preventing electrical interference while allowing for higher component density on chips. Industry experts note that this technology is crucial for maintaining Moore's Law trajectory as manufacturers push toward 5nm processes and beyond."The refined STI approach enables better control of leakage current and parasitic capacitance," explains Dr. Sarah Chen, semiconductor process engineer. "This translates directly to improved power efficiency in consumer electronics."The innovation comes as chipmakers face mounting challenges in balancing performance demands with thermal constraints in increasingly compact devices.

Investigation of Nodal Domains in the Chaotic Microwave Ray-Splitting Rough BilliardWe study experimentally nodal domains of wave functions (electric field distributions) in the chaotic microwave ray-splitting rough billiard. This billiard, characterized by a rough boundary, functions as a microscale domain where the trajectories of microwaves become highly convoluted and unpredictable. The nodal domains, the regions where the wave function is zero, are of particular interest as they reveal the intricate patterns of wave interference and the underlying chaotic dynamics of the system.In our setup, the billiard is illuminated by microwaves, and the electric field is mapped using a high-resolution imaging technique. By analyzing the nodal domains, we uncover the complex interplay between the geometry of the boundary and the wave propagation. The chaotic nature of the billiard ensures that the nodal lines do not form simple, predictable patterns but instead create a rich tapestry of interwoven domains.Our findings suggest that the distribution and topology of the nodal domains are closely tied to the spectral properties of the billiard, providing a window into the quantum behavior of chaotic systems. This study not only deepens our understanding of wave dynamics in complex geometries but also has potential implications for the design of novel optical and electronic devices.

The herd behavior of returns is investigated in Korean futures markets. It is obtained that the probability distribution of returns for three types of herders – fundamentalists, momentum traders, and noise traders – exhibits distinct characteristics compared to a normal distribution. Fundamentalists, who rely on technical and fundamental analysis, show returns with fatter tails, indicating lower volatility and less clustered behavior. Momentum traders, driven by the belief in continuation of trends, exhibit fatter tails and higher leptokurtosis, suggesting more extreme events and clustered returns. Noise traders, who act on irrational emotions and short-term speculation, show the most fatter tails and higher kurtosis, contributing to market unpredictability.This study highlights the importance of understanding the different herding mechanisms in Korean futures markets, as they significantly influence market dynamics and risk. The findings suggest that the fat-tailed distribution and clustered behavior of returns pose challenges for traditional risk management models. Furthermore, the high kurtosis observed in noise traders’ returns indicates the need for regulatory interventions to mitigate market volatility. This critical analysis contributes to a deeper understanding of herding behavior in financial markets and its implications for investors and regulators.

# PI3K/Akt/mTOR inhibitors in cancer: At the bench and bedside.Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) pathway is one of the most frequently dysregulated pathways in cancer. Let's talk about why it's such a hot target in oncology research today.When we look at this signaling cascade, it's like a cellular command center controlling cell growth, survival, and metabolism. The beauty of targeting PI3K/Akt/mTOR is that it hits cancer at multiple levels.In the lab, researchers have shown remarkable results with these inhibitors across various cancer types. They're seeing tumor shrinkage, decreased metastasis, and even reversal of drug resistance in some cases.At the bedside, we now have several FDA-approved drugs like everolimus, temsirolimus, and alpelisib making real differences for patients. But it's not all smooth sailing - we're still wrestling with toxicity issues, resistance mechanisms, and identifying the right biomarkers for patient selection.The future? It's about smarter combinations and more precise targeting. The PI3K story is still being written.

As quantum technology advances, the refinement and application of such aperiodic DD sequences will continue to be pivotal in achieving reliable and scalable quantum computing systems.

# Adaptive Parameter-Free Bandit AlgorithmsExisting strategies for finite-armed stochastic bandits mostly depend on a parameter of scale that must be known in advance. Sometimes this is in the form of a bound on the rewards, other times as a confidence level or horizon. This dependence creates a practical dilemma: underestimating these parameters leads to poor performance, while overestimating them results in unnecessarily slow learning.Recent advances have introduced parameter-free algorithms that adapt automatically to unknown reward ranges. These methods employ doubling tricks or adaptive confidence bounds that self-calibrate as more data becomes available. By dynamically adjusting exploration rates, they achieve near-optimal regret without prior knowledge of the environment's scale.This adaptive approach represents a significant step toward more practical reinforcement learning systems that can be deployed with minimal tuning. As bandits find applications in increasingly diverse domains from healthcare to finance, algorithms that require less expert configuration become essential for widespread adoption.

The findings suggest that activation of the superior sagittal sinus, potentially mimicking the effects of headache-inducing stimuli, elicits a specific neuronal response pattern. This study provides valuable insights into the neural pathways involved in dural pain processing and may contribute to a better understanding of migraine and other headache disorders.

By integrating adaptive feedback control with real-time digital signal processing, the method achieves simultaneous tuning of amplitude and phase with sub-nanosecond latency, ensuring minimal field distortion. Such precision is vital for applications like particle accelerators and quantum computing systems, where even minor fluctuations can degrade performance. The proposed architecture employs a hybrid approach, combining PID controllers with machine learning algorithms to predict and correct deviations caused by thermal drift or mechanical vibrations. Experimental validation using a 1.3 GHz SRF cavity demonstrated a 40% improvement in field stability compared to conventional phase-locked loops. Furthermore, the system’s FPGA-based implementation ensures scalability for multi-cavity arrays. This innovation not only enhances operational reliability but also reduces energy consumption by optimizing field uniformity. Future work will explore applications in quantum metamaterials and next-generation communication systems, underscoring its transformative potential in RF engineering.

Derivatives of semi-synthetic diosmine in the treatment of patients with chronic venous insufficiency. The results of a prospective study—using pharmacological agents derived from diosmine, a phytochemical with venotonic properties, have shown promise in managing chronic venous insufficiency (CVI), a condition characterized by impaired venous return and leg discomfort. A recent prospective study evaluated the efficacy and safety of a novel semi-synthetic diosmine derivative in 200 CVI patients over 12 weeks. Participants reported significant reductions in edema, pain, and nocturnal leg cramps compared to placebo, with minimal adverse effects. The compound’s mechanism likely involves enhancing vascular tone, improving microcirculation, and reinforcing capillary permeability. Unlike traditional therapies, which may cause gastrointestinal irritation, this derivative demonstrated superior tolerability. The study underscores its potential as a first-line option for early-stage CVI, though larger trials are needed to confirm long-term benefits. These findings highlight the therapeutic value of semi-synthetic phytochemicals in addressing vascular disorders, offering a safer alternative to conventional treatments. (150 words)

Sulfation of minoxidil by human liver phenol sulfotransferase. The N,O-sulfate of minoxidil (Mnx) is a critical metabolic pathway that influences the drug's pharmacokinetics and therapeutic efficacy. Minoxidil, primarily used for the treatment of hypertension and androgenetic alopecia, undergoes sulfation in the liver, catalyzed by phenol sulfotransferase enzymes. This enzymatic reaction results in the formation of Mnx, which is more water-soluble and facilitates the drug's excretion.The sulfation process not only affects the bioavailability of minoxidil but also plays a role in its mechanism of action. Studies have shown that the sulfated metabolite retains some biological activity, contributing to the overall therapeutic effects of the drug. Understanding the sulfation of minoxidil is essential for optimizing its clinical use and for developing new derivatives with improved pharmacodynamic properties. Further research into the enzymatic pathways involved in minoxidil metabolism could lead to enhanced treatment strategies for patients.

Tied links and the tied braid monoid were introduced recently by the authors and used to define new invariants for classical links. In this work, we further explore these concepts, utilizing the tied braid monoid's structure to construct a novel invariant for tied links. This invariant, built upon the combinatorial properties of tied braids, offers a fresh perspective on distinguishing tied links, which are a generalization of classical links allowing for additional connections and complexities.The tied braid monoid extends the concept of braid groups by incorporating "ties" between strands, thereby enriching the algebraic framework for studying links. By defining invariants based on these tied braids, we aim to capture more nuanced topological information that classical invariants might overlook. Our combinatorial approach focuses on the algebraic properties of tied braids, providing a systematic method for computation and comparison.This work aligns with the established use of braid groups in knot theory, where invariants derived from braids have proven invaluable in distinguishing knots and links. By leveraging the tied braid monoid, we extend this methodology to a broader class of links, potentially uncovering new relationships and equivalences within knot theory. Our findings suggest that these new invariants could lead to a deeper understanding of tied links' topology, with implications for both theoretical and applied knot theory.

Hand function, experienced pain, and disability after distal radius fracture. We sought to explore differences in range of motion (ROM), grip strength, and self-reported outcomes between patients treated surgically versus non-surgically. Distal radius fractures are common injuries, but recovery can be unpredictable, leaving many with lingering issues. Our study compared 60 patients—30 who underwent surgical fixation and 30 managed with casting—assessing their progress at 6 and 12 months post-injury. Results showed both groups regained similar wrist ROM by 12 months, but grip strength lagged in surgically treated patients, possibly due to prolonged immobilization or scar tissue. Surprisingly, self-reported disability (measured via patient-rated wrist evaluations) was higher in non-surgical patients, despite comparable physical metrics. This highlights a disconnect between objective measures and patients’ perceived function—a critical consideration for care. Pain scores improved steadily over time but remained elevated in both groups, emphasizing the need for targeted pain management. Clinicians should prioritize early mobility exercises and strength training, even after surgery, to bridge the gap between physical recovery and patient satisfaction. Our findings underscore that recovery is multifaceted, and personalized rehab plans are key to minimizing long-term disability.

# A method and system for generating robust XPath expressions for a selected node in transcodable markupA method and system for generating robust XPath expressions for a selected node in transcodable markup. The system of the invention can include a set of differing algorithms to generate alternative XPath expressions with varying levels of specificity and resilience. These expressions are designed to maintain node identification integrity even when the underlying document structure undergoes modification during transcoding processes.The methodology employs attribute-based identification, positional referencing, and structural context analysis to create redundant addressing mechanisms. When implemented in web automation frameworks or content extraction systems, this approach significantly reduces the failure rate of node selection operations.The system evaluates generated XPath expressions against potential document transformations, calculating a robustness score for each expression. This quantitative assessment enables the selection of optimal expressions for specific use cases, balancing precision with adaptability to structural changes in the markup.

A hypodermic syringe and method of filling the syringe with an injection fluid. The syringe includes a fluid chamber for retaining an injection fluid and a plunger that allows for precise control when administering medication. This device is essential in both clinical settings and at home for self-administration. To fill the syringe, first, ensure that the needle is sterile and securely attached. Then, submerge the needle into the vial containing the injection fluid. Pull the plunger back gently, creating a vacuum that draws the medication into the fluid chamber. It’s crucial to eliminate air bubbles by lightly tapping the syringe and pushing the plunger slightly to expel any trapped air. Once filled, the syringe is ready for use. Remember to follow safety protocols to avoid contamination. This simple yet effective method of filling hypodermic syringes plays a vital role in modern medicine, ensuring accurate and safe delivery of treatments.

**Echinococcus granulosus (Taeniidae) and autochthonous echinococcosis in a North American horse.** We report the first documented case of autochthonous cystic echinococcosis in a North American horse, underscoring emerging zoonotic risks in non-endemic regions. *Echinococcus granulosus*, a tapeworm typically found in canids (definitive hosts) and livestock (intermediate hosts), forms hydatid cysts in organs, posing severe health threats. While human infections are rare in North America, this case highlights potential local transmission cycles, likely involving wildlife reservoirs or domestic dogs. The horse, residing in the Pacific Northwest, presented with hepatic cysts confirmed via histopathology and molecular analysis. Traditionally, North American echinococcosis cases are linked to imported infections or sylvatic cycles involving wolves and elk. This finding challenges assumptions about geographic restrictions and emphasizes the parasite’s adaptability. Public health implications are significant, as undetected infections in livestock or pets could facilitate human exposure. Veterinary surveillance and owner education on deworming protocols are critical to mitigate risks. Climate change and shifting wildlife populations may further alter parasite distribution, warranting proactive monitoring. This case serves as a reminder of evolving zoonotic landscapes and the need for interdisciplinary collaboration in One Health initiatives.

A southern Ontario man’s drunken swim touched off an international rescue operation late Monday night, police say. The 47-year-old Windsor, Ont., man made his way to the Detroit River’s Canadian shoreline around 11 p.m., where he reportedly entered the water despite icy temperatures and strong currents. Authorities say he began swimming toward the U.S. side, prompting a frantic 911 call from a bystander. Windsor police, the Canadian Coast Guard, and the U.S. Customs and Border Protection were quickly mobilized. A U.S. Coast Guard helicopter and a Canadian rescue boat converged on the river, coordinating a search that spanned both countries. After 90 minutes, the man was located near Detroit’s Ambassador Bridge and hoisted aboard the helicopter. He suffered no serious injuries but faced charges in Canada for public intoxication and obstructing police. “This highlights the dangers of impaired judgment in hazardous conditions,” said Windsor Police spokesperson Constable Jason Barton. The incident underscores the rare collaboration required when emergencies cross borders, even on a frigid winter night.

The influence of mechanical strain on the critical current (Ic) is investigated for MgB2/stainless steel (SUS316) superconducting composites. By applying mechanical strain, researchers aim to understand how external forces affect the superconducting properties of MgB2, a material known for its high critical temperature and potential for practical applications. Initial findings suggest that moderate strain can enhance the critical current, potentially improving the performance and efficiency of these composites. However, excessive strain can lead to degradation, highlighting the importance of precise control in practical applications. This research offers valuable insights into optimizing the integration of superconducting materials in engineering designs.

Sporadic amplification of the MYC gene in human osteosarcomas.The MYC proto-oncogene has been shown to be overexpressed in a variety of human cancers, including osteosarcomas. Amplification of the MYC gene, resulting in increased transcription and subsequent overproduction of the MYC protein, has been identified as a key driver of tumorigenesis in osteosarcoma cells. This aberrant expression of MYC is thought to contribute to the aggressive growth and metastatic potential of osteosarcoma tumors.Studies have consistently demonstrated that increased MYC protein levels are associated with poor prognosis and reduced overall survival in patients with osteosarcoma. Furthermore, MYC amplification has been observed in a subset of high-grade osteosarcomas, suggesting a potential role for MYC as a biomarker for aggressive disease.Research into the molecular mechanisms underlying MYC-driven osteosarcoma is ongoing, with potential therapeutic targets for intervention being explored. Understanding the role of MYC in osteosarcoma pathogenesis is crucial for the development of effective treatments and improving patient outcomes.

Two hundred people were invited to the reception including members of the emergency services, the Manx Electricity Authority and farmers. Adam Wood said: "The weather has been a relentless adversary this year, but today we celebrate our collective resilience." The event, held in the shadow of the Isle of Man’s rugged landscape, marked the recovery from a devastating storm that left thousands without power and farms cut off by landslides just weeks prior. Wood, a project coordinator for the island’s infrastructure initiative, emphasized collaboration. "When the gales hit, it wasn’t just engineers fixing lines or firefighters clearing debris—it was farmers opening fields as emergency routes and electricians sleeping in trucks to restart grids at dawn," he said. Local farmer Eilidh MacLean nodded in agreement. "We’re all threads in the same net here. Without the grid team restoring power, my dairy herd would’ve suffered. Without the police directing traffic, supplies couldn’t reach remote areas." The evening’s speeches wove a narrative of shared responsibility, underscored by a video montage of storm-damaged fields now blooming with fresh crops. As attendees raised glasses to "preparedness and grit," it was clear the real victory lay not in conquering the weather, but in uniting under it.

Diabetes, obesity and gut microbiota. The gut microbiota composition has been associated with several hallmarks of metabolic syndrome (e.g., obesity, type 2 diabetes). This dysbiosis can influence energy harvesting from food, contributing to weight gain. Furthermore, certain gut bacteria can promote inflammation, leading to insulin resistance, a key feature of type 2 diabetes.Targeting the gut microbiota through dietary interventions, prebiotics, probiotics, and even fecal microbiota transplantation, represents a promising avenue for mitigating metabolic disorders. Further investigation into the specific microbial species and their metabolic pathways will be crucial for developing effective therapeutic strategies. Ultimately, understanding the intricate relationship between the gut microbiome, obesity, and diabetes could revolutionize preventative and therapeutic approaches.

Substance dependence and eating disorders: impact of sequence on comorbidity. There is a high comorbidity between eating disorders and substance dependence. The sequence in which these conditions develop profoundly influences their clinical trajectory, severity, and treatment outcomes—a critical yet underemphasized aspect of comorbidity. Research underscores that the temporal relationship between the two disorders shapes their psychological and neurobiological interplay. For instance, individuals with preexisting eating disorders often use substances to suppress appetite or cope with body dissatisfaction, exacerbating addiction risks. Conversely, substance misuse can trigger disordered eating behaviors, such as bingeing or purging, as users attempt to mitigate drug-related weight gain or emotional distress. The directionality of this relationship matters: those with eating disorders preceding substance use typically exhibit poorer prognoses, with heightened rates of relapse and psychiatric complications. Neurobiological overlaps, such as dysregulated dopamine pathways, further complicate this bidirectional dynamic. However, treatment strategies often conflate the two disorders, neglecting the need for tailored interventions based on onset order. Prioritizing the primary disorder in sequential treatment plans could improve outcomes, yet this approach remains underutilized. Failing to address the sequence perpetuates a cycle of mismanagement, underscoring the urgency of integrating temporal analysis into clinical frameworks.

In situ hybridisation in filamentous fungi using peptide nucleic acid probes. Fluorescent DNA and peptide nucleic acid (PNA) probes were employed to visualize specific RNA molecules within the intricate cellular structures of filamentous fungi. This technique allowed researchers to pinpoint the localization of transcripts involved in various cellular processes, offering unprecedented insights into gene expression dynamics. Peptide nucleic acids, with their unique backbone structure, proved particularly advantageous due to their enhanced resistance to nuclease degradation and their superior binding affinity to complementary RNA sequences. The combination of PNA probes and fluorescence microscopy revealed detailed spatial and temporal patterns of RNA distribution, highlighting the dynamic nature of fungal gene regulation. This approach not only expanded our understanding of fungal biology but also paved the way for more sophisticated studies on gene function and regulation in these complex organisms.

[Guillain-Barré syndrome in the adult: therapeutic aspects]. The Guillain-Barré syndrome is the most common cause of acute flaccid paralysis in adults, and it can be quite alarming. This syndrome occurs when the immune system mistakenly attacks the peripheral nerves, leading to muscle weakness and, in some cases, paralysis. When it comes to treatment, early intervention is key. Two primary therapies are often employed: intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) and plasma exchange. IVIG helps by providing antibodies that can reduce the immune response, while plasma exchange removes harmful antibodies from the blood. Both treatments aim to speed up recovery and reduce the severity of symptoms.Supportive care is also crucial. This includes physical therapy to help regain strength and mobility, as well as monitoring respiratory function, since some patients may need assistance with breathing. Overall, with timely treatment and rehabilitation, many individuals can experience significant recovery, although the road to full health can be lengthy.

Integrability and chaos are two of the main concepts associated with nonlinear physical systems which have revolutionized our understanding of them. Highly stable, exponentially localized solitons are fascinating solutions that emerge from such systems, showcasing the delicate balance between order and unpredictability. Integrable systems, characterized by their solvability through analytical methods, often host these solitons, which maintain their shape and speed even after interactions. This predictability contrasts starkly with chaotic systems, where sensitivity to initial conditions leads to seemingly random behavior.Solitons, first observed in shallow water waves, are now pivotal in various fields, from optical fibers to quantum mechanics. Their stability and localization offer practical applications, such as in data transmission, where they can travel long distances without distortion. Meanwhile, chaos theory has provided insights into complex systems, from weather patterns to the stock market, revealing underlying structures in apparent randomness. Together, integrability and chaos underscore the intricate tapestry of nonlinear systems, bridging the gap between order and disorder.

We introduce a technique of time series analysis, potential forecasting, which is based on dynamical propagation of the probability density of time series. We employ polynomial expansions to approximate the underlying dynamics, enabling us to capture complex patterns and trends that traditional methods might overlook. This approach leverages the idea that the evolution of a time series can be modeled as a flow in a potential landscape, where the probability density evolves according to a set of governing equations. By estimating the potential function, we can predict future states with greater accuracy, even in the presence of noise or irregular fluctuations.Potential forecasting is particularly useful in scenarios where the data exhibits non-linear behavior or abrupt changes, such as financial markets, climate systems, or biological processes. The method provides a robust framework for uncertainty quantification, offering not only point forecasts but also confidence intervals. This makes it a valuable tool for decision-making in fields where risk assessment is critical. Our initial experiments demonstrate promising results, showcasing its ability to outperform conventional forecasting techniques in both accuracy and interpretability.

Researchers have conducted in vitro analyses to investigate the promoter activity of the liver-type arginase gene, focusing on its regulation and expression under various conditions. In vitro experiments have shown that this promoter is highly responsive to liver-specific signals, ensuring that arginase expression is tightly regulated in a liver-dependent manner. This promoter is also subject to post-transcriptional regulation, further modulating its activity in different cellular contexts. Understanding the promoter activity of liver-type arginase provides insights into the regulation of urea cycle enzymes in the liver. This knowledge is critical for studying liver function, ammonia detoxification, and the pathophysiology of liver diseases. By analyzing the promoter in vitro, researchers aim to uncover mechanisms that could be targeted for therapeutic interventions in metabolic disorders.

**High-resolution alpha spectrometry under field conditions - fast identification of alpha particle emitting radionuclides from air samples.** Alpha particle emitting radionuclides may be insidious threats, lurking in environmental or nuclear accident scenarios. While traditional laboratory-based spectrometry offers precision, its reliance on controlled settings and prolonged analysis undermines urgent response needs. Modern portable systems promise rapid, on-site detection of isotopes like plutonium-239 or uranium-238, leveraging advanced semiconductor detectors and real-time data processing. Yet, this innovation warrants scrutiny. Field spectrometers, though revolutionary, grapple with compromises. Energy resolution—critical for distinguishing closely overlapping alpha peaks—often falters in rugged environments, risking misidentification in complex samples. Calibration drifts due to temperature fluctuations or humidity further challenge reliability. Moreover, the touted “speed” may come at the cost of sensitivity, potentially overlooking low-concentration radionuclides in favor of dominant signals. While these devices empower first responders, their deployment demands rigorous validation. Overconfidence in field results could delay lab confirmation, exacerbating public health risks. The balance between portability and accuracy remains precarious. As nuclear industries and environmental monitoring evolve, so must the transparency around these tools’ limitations. Progress, yes—but with measured skepticism.

The integration of liquid biopsy into clinical practice has the potential to transform the management of NSCLC, enabling more personalized and effective treatment strategies.

# Methods for choosing the regularization parameter and estimating the noise variance in image restoration and their relation.The application of regularization to ill-conditioned problems necessitates the difficult task of selecting an optimal regularization parameter. In my experience, this choice dramatically impacts the quality of restored images. I've found that methods like generalized cross-validation (GCV) and the L-curve approach offer practical solutions, though they're far from perfect.What fascinates me is the intimate relationship between regularization parameter selection and noise variance estimation. These two aspects form a delicate dance in the restoration process. When I underestimate noise variance, I invariably select too small a regularization parameter, resulting in noise amplification. Conversely, overestimation leads to excessive smoothing and loss of crucial details.I believe the discrepancy principle provides the most intuitive approach when noise statistics are available, though in real-world applications, this information is rarely at hand, making the problem substantially more challenging.

Stochastic Gradient Markov Chain Monte Carlo (SG-MCMC) algorithms have become increasingly popular for Bayesian inference in large-scale applications. Even though these methods offer significant computational advantages over traditional MCMC, they introduce biases due to stochastic gradients. This bias, a consequence of using mini-batches of data, can lead to inaccurate posterior approximations.Recent research focuses on mitigating this bias. Proposed solutions include variance reduction techniques, which aim to reduce the variance of the stochastic gradients, and control variates, which introduce a control variate to correct the bias. Additionally, adaptive step-size schemes are being developed to optimize the convergence of SG-MCMC algorithms. The ongoing development of SG-MCMC methods addresses the trade-off between computational efficiency and accuracy, making them a crucial area of study for modern Bayesian statistics.

We consider a problem in eigenvalue optimization, in particular finding a local minimizer of the spectral abscissa—the value of a parameter that results in the smallest real part of the eigenvalues of a given matrix. This problem, while fundamental in control theory and dynamical systems, presents significant challenges due to its non-convex nature. Traditional optimization techniques often struggle to find global minimizers efficiently, as local minima can trap algorithms, leading to suboptimal solutions.Recent advances in numerical methods and algorithms have shown promise in navigating these complexities. However, the landscape of the spectral abscissa function remains intricate, with sharp changes and multiple local minima. This makes the task of identifying a robust local minimizer not only computationally intensive but also theoretically challenging.Moreover, the sensitivity of the spectral abscissa to perturbations in the matrix entries adds another layer of difficulty. Small changes can lead to dramatic shifts in the eigenvalue structure, complicating the optimization process. Thus, while progress has been made, the problem of finding a reliable local minimizer of the spectral abscissa remains a critical and open area in mathematical optimization.

[Evaluation of various hemorheologic parameters in diabetes mellitus] It has been speculated that changes in intrinsic blood flow properties may contribute to the evolution and progression of diabetic microvascular complications. This study investigates the relationship between several hemorheologic parameters and glycemic control in a cohort of individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Parameters assessed include blood viscosity at varying shear rates, erythrocyte aggregation, and red blood cell deformability.Preliminary findings indicate a statistically significant positive correlation between glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels and increased blood viscosity, particularly at low shear rates. Furthermore, decreased erythrocyte deformability was observed in participants with poorer glycemic control. These results suggest that altered hemorheologic properties may be a significant factor in the development of diabetic microangiopathy. Further investigation is warranted to elucidate the underlying mechanisms and explore potential therapeutic interventions targeting hemorheologic abnormalities.

Bitches, queens and prostaglandins. Luteolysis can be obtained in bitches by prolonged administration of PGF2 alpha, resulting in abortion. In the world of canine reproduction, PGF2 alpha (prostaglandin F2 alpha) plays a crucial role. It's often used in veterinary practice to induce luteolysis, which is the process of ending the function of the corpus luteum, leading to the onset of estrus or, in some cases, abortion.For queens (female cats), PGF2 alpha is also a powerful tool used to synchronize estrus cycles, aiding in breeding programs. However, in bitches (female dogs), its application is more focused on managing luteal function. By administering PGF2 alpha over an extended period, veterinarians can trigger luteolysis, effectively ending the pregnancy and allowing the bitch to return to estrus.This technique is particularly useful in managing unwanted pregnancies or when breeders need to control the breeding cycle. However, it's a delicate procedure requiring careful monitoring to ensure the health and well-being of the bitch.

Here's the article:We show that a diagonalizable (non-Hermitian) Hamiltonian H is pseudo-Hermitian if and only if it has an antilinear symmetry. This means that the Hamiltonian has a specific property that allows it to relate to its complex conjugate in a particular way.Now, let's break this down. A Hamiltonian is a mathematical object that describes the dynamics of a system. In quantum mechanics, it's a crucial component that determines the time-evolution of a system. When we say that H is diagonalizable, we mean that it can be expressed as a sum of its eigenvalues and eigenvectors. However, this doesn't necessarily mean that H is Hermitian, which is a property that requires the Hamiltonian to be equal to its own complex conjugate.So, what's the connection between diagonalizability and pseudo-Hermiticity? Well, if H is diagonalizable, then it has an antilinear symmetry, which means that it's related to its complex conjugate in a way that's analogous to how a Hermitian operator is related to its adjoint. This has profound implications for the study of non-Hermitian Hamiltonians and their properties.

# This article solves an optimal control problem arising in attitude control of a spacecraft under state and control constraints. We first derive the discrete-time attitude dynamics by employing quaternion representation and Euler's rotational equations. The resulting nonlinear system presents unique challenges when incorporating realistic operational constraints.Our approach utilizes a novel pseudospectral method that transforms the constrained optimization problem into a nonlinear programming problem solvable via sequential quadratic programming. Unlike conventional methods, we incorporate both pointing requirements and actuator limitations directly into the formulation.Numerical simulations demonstrate the efficacy of our approach for a CubeSat reorientation maneuver. Results show a 23% reduction in control effort compared to benchmark methods while maintaining pointing accuracy within 0.05 degrees. The algorithm converges reliably even under severe initial attitude errors.This methodology offers promising applications for resource-limited spacecraft missions where fuel efficiency and constraint satisfaction are paramount considerations.

# A Parabolic Determinant Line Bundle on the Moduli Space of Stable Parabolic BundlesIn \cite{BR1}, \cite{BR2}, a parabolic determinant line bundle on a moduli space of stable parabolic bundles was constructed and studied extensively. This mathematical object plays a crucial role in understanding the geometry of moduli spaces associated with vector bundles on curves with parabolic structures at marked points.The construction generalizes the classical determinant line bundle to the parabolic setting, incorporating weights at the parabolic points. These weights determine the stability condition for parabolic bundles and influence the geometric properties of the resulting moduli space.Analysis of this line bundle reveals its connection to parabolic cohomology and its significance in computing intersection numbers on the moduli space. The authors demonstrate that the first Chern class of this parabolic determinant bundle can be expressed in terms of the parabolic degree and rank, providing a natural extension of the non-parabolic case.

Unlike electronic counterparts vulnerable to hacking or power failures, a well-constructed pawl engages seamlessly with the latch bolt, ensuring fail-safe operation through purely mechanical force. Advocates for mechanical latches must therefore prioritize rigorous manufacturing standards and regular maintenance. For instance, wear on the pawl’s engagement surface can degrade performance over time, demanding proactive inspection. Dismissing such systems as obsolete ignores their irreplaceable role in emergency egress and durability under stress. In fire scenarios or structural shifts, a robust latch bolt and pawl withstand forces that might cripple electronic mechanisms. Innovation should enhance, not replace, these time-tested designs—ensuring security remains both intelligent and impervious to failure. **Early stage prostate cancer: biochemical recurrence after treatment.** To identify retrospectively through chart analysis the biochemical recurrence frequency of localized prostate cancer at diagnosis of patients submitted to radical prostatectomy or radiation therapy, a comprehensive review was conducted. The study revealed that biochemical recurrence, defined as a rising prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level after initial treatment, remains a significant concern. Among the patients analyzed, approximately 20-30% experienced recurrence within five years post-treatment. This recurrence often serves as an early indicator of potential disease progression, even in the absence of clinical symptoms.The data highlighted that factors such as Gleason score, preoperative PSA levels, and surgical margins played pivotal roles in predicting recurrence. Patients with higher Gleason scores or positive surgical margins were more likely to experience biochemical failure. Radiation therapy patients also showed similar recurrence patterns, with dose intensity and treatment adherence influencing outcomes.These findings underscore the importance of vigilant post-treatment monitoring and personalized follow-up strategies. Early detection of biochemical recurrence allows for timely intervention, potentially improving long-term survival and quality of life for prostate cancer patients.

Local mode mixity and stress triaxiality play an important role during metal/ceramic interface fracture. It has been reported in the literature that these parameters govern the propagation of cracks at the interface, where dissimilar materials meet. The interplay between mixed-mode fracture (a blend of opening, sliding, and tearing stresses) and highly constrained stress states amplifies the complexity of failure mechanisms. Imagine a ceramic coating bonded to a metal substrate under load—microscopic stress concentrations at the interface create a battleground where material stiffness mismatches and geometric irregularities conspire to steer crack paths. Stress triaxiality, the degree of compressive confinement around a crack tip, acts like a double-edged sword: while it can blunt crack growth in uniaxial tension, mixed-mode shear stresses exploit weak spots, fracturing bonds like a pickax on fragile glaze. Researchers have observed that even minor variations in local stress distributions—triggered by surface roughness or residual strains—can drastically alter fracture toughness. These insights are vital for designing next-gen composites, where tailoring interface architectures to balance stress triaxiality and mode mixity could unlock stronger, longer-lasting materials for aerospace and biomedical applications. The dance of stress and structure at the nanoscale remains a compelling frontier in fracture mechanics. (150 words)

The current dominant paradigm in sensorimotor control, whether imitation or reinforcement learning, is to train policies directly in raw action spaces such as torque, joint angles, or even muscle activations. While appealing in its apparent simplicity, directly manipulating low-level motor commands bypasses the rich hierarchical structure inherent in biological motor control. We are not puppeteers pulling individual muscle strings. Instead, we orchestrate movement through learned, high-level motor primitives – sequences of actions combined into reusable skills.Training policies directly on raw actions results in brittle, inefficient learning. Each new task necessitates retraining from scratch, failing to leverage existing motor repertoire. Furthermore, the resulting policies are often non-robust, sensitive to noise and unexpected perturbations. By focusing on high-level skills, we can achieve greater generalization, faster adaptation, and more robust control, ultimately mirroring the adaptability and grace we observe in natural movement. The future of sensorimotor control lies not in brute-force optimization, but in embracing hierarchical abstraction.

The continuum theory of domain structures in ferromagnetic/superconducting bilayers fails when the equilibrium domain size becomes comparable with the effective penetration depth. Now, what does that even mean? Let's break it down. When you've got a ferromagnetic and a superconducting material stacked on top of each other, you'd expect the magnetic domains to form in a pretty predictable way. But nope, it turns out those domains can behave erratically when their size gets close to the distance that the magnetic field can penetrate into the superconductor. That's the effective penetration depth we're talking about here. It's a crucial length scale that determines how the magnetic field interacts with the superconductor. When the domain size gets too close to this length scale, the continuum theory just can't keep up. It's like trying to predict the behavior of a chaotic system with a simple mathematical model. It just doesn't work.

A method for growing carbon nanowalls on a base material is disclosed. The method comprises mixing a predetermined amount of a hydrocarbon gas with a predetermined ratio of a carrier gas, such as hydrogen or argon, to create a reactive atmosphere. This gas mixture is then introduced into a chemical vapor deposition (CVD) chamber where a substrate, typically a silicon wafer or metal alloy, is heated to a high temperature. A catalyst, often a transition metal like nickel or iron, is deposited onto the substrate to initiate the nucleation of carbon structures. Under controlled pressure and temperature conditions, the hydrocarbon molecules decompose, and carbon atoms assemble vertically along the substrate, forming graphene-like sheets—nanowalls—that stand perpendicular to the surface. The process’s precision lies in balancing gas flow rates and thermal parameters to optimize wall thickness, height, and density. The resulting nanowalls exhibit exceptional surface area and mechanical stability, making them ideal for applications in energy storage, sensors, and nanoelectronics. This innovation simplifies the synthesis of two-dimensional carbon architectures while expanding their practical utility in high-performance technologies.

**Paget Disease of the Spine** Seventy patients who had the radiographic features of Paget disease of the spine were evaluated clinically and with computed tomography (CT). This retrospective analysis aimed to correlate imaging findings with clinical manifestations and complications. Participants, aged 52–85 years (mean 68.5), comprised 42 males and 28 females. Clinical assessment revealed persistent back pain in 89% (n=62), neurological deficits (e.g., radiculopathy, myelopathy) in 34% (n=24), and spinal deformities in 41% (n=29). CT imaging demonstrated characteristic bony abnormalities, including vertebral enlargement (94%), mixed lytic-sclerotic lesions (82%), and cortical thickening (76%). Notably, 19 patients (27%) exhibited complications such as spinal stenosis (n=15) and pathological fractures (n=4). Structural compromise of neural foramina was identified in 21 cases (30%), correlating strongly with neurological symptoms (p<0.01). These findings underscore CT’s superiority over conventional radiography in delineating osseous detail and complications. Early detection of spinal stenosis or fractures via CT facilitates timely intervention, potentially mitigating neurological deterioration. This study highlights the importance of integrating advanced imaging into the diagnostic workflow for Paget disease of the spine, emphasizing its role in guiding clinical management and improving patient outcomes.

**A Wireless Router-Assisted Security Handoff Method** In modern wireless networks, ensuring seamless and secure communication is critical, especially in infrastructure-based mobile multi-hop networks. This method leverages an efficient layer 2 security handoff mechanism, which operates on top of the data link layer. By integrating wireless routers into the process, the system achieves faster and more reliable handoffs between access points. The layer 2 approach ensures that data is encrypted and authenticated at the packet level, reducing the risk of unauthorized access and ensuring data integrity. The proposed method also minimizes latency and enhances overall network performance. By offloading some of the security responsibilities to the wireless router, the system can handle multiple handoffs simultaneously without compromising security. This is particularly beneficial for infrastructure-based mobile networks, where multi-hop communication is common. In summary, the **wireless router-assisted security handoff method** offers a robust and efficient solution for securing communication in complex wireless environments. Its ability to integrate seamlessly with layer 2 protocols makes it a valuable addition to modern network infrastructure.

The acetylated form showed comparable absorption but slightly different excretion patterns, suggesting varied metabolic fate.**Implications**: The study highlights the role of L-methionine and its acetylated form in infant nutrition. Understanding their metabolism could aid in developing tailored dietary recommendations for optimal growth and development. This research underscores the importance of methionine in early nutrition, paving the way for future studies on its applications in paediatric care.

Recent research suggests that these receptors might be potential therapeutic targets for conditions like type 2 diabetes and obesity. By modulating glucagon receptor activity, it may be possible to control excessive glucose production, thus aiding in better management of blood sugar levels. However, challenges remain in developing drugs that can selectively target these receptors without eliciting adverse effects. As understanding deepens, glucagon receptors continue to be at the forefront of metabolic research.

# Novel $ADE$ Correspondences Through Combined Theoretical FrameworksIn this paper we present novel $ADE$ correspondences by combining an earlier induction theorem of ours with one of Arnold's observations concerning Trinities. The intersection of these theoretical frameworks yields unexpected connections between Dynkin diagrams and certain singularity classifications previously considered unrelated.Our approach extends the classical McKay correspondence by incorporating Arnold's Trinity principle, which links exceptional Lie algebras with specific families of singularities. By applying our induction method to these structures, we demonstrate that the resulting correspondences form coherent patterns across multiple mathematical domains.The significance of these findings lies in their potential applications to algebraic geometry, representation theory, and mathematical physics. Particularly noteworthy is how these correspondences illuminate the underlying symmetries of moduli spaces associated with certain quantum field theories.This work opens avenues for further research into the deep structural connections between seemingly disparate mathematical objects unified through the $ADE$ classification paradigm.

Conformational changes in iota- and kappa-carrageenans induced by complex formation with bovine beta-casein. The formation of electrostatic interactions between these carrageenan types and beta-casein is a fascinating area of study. When iota-carrageenan, known for its high affinity for cations and its strong gel-forming ability, interacts with beta-casein in an aqueous solution, its linear backbone rearranges to form a more compact, helical structure. This change is driven by the electrostatic attraction between the negatively charged sulfate and carboxylic acid groups in the carrageenan and the positively charged lysine and histidine residues in beta-casein.Kappa-carrageenan, on the other hand, has a lower sulfate content, which means it forms milder complexes. Its conformational change is less dramatic but still involves some degree of rearrangement, leading to a slightly altered hydration shell and reduced solubility. These interactions not only affect the physical properties of the carrageenan but also have implications in food science, where they can influence the texture and stability of dairy products.
